title: Regional capacity safety margins & gating heuristics — field trials
summary: Notes and raw results from a set of field trials that tested region-specific capacity safety margins and scale gating heuristics. Goal: reduce unnecessary scale-ups while keeping p95 token latency under SLO and limiting cold-start failures during burst events.
experiment_goals: 1) Quantify impact of per-region safety margin reduction (10% -> 0%) on cost and p95 latency. 2) Evaluate gating conditions (queue-length vs request-rate vs recent-loss) for scale-up. 3) Validate cooldown/hysteresis settings that avoid oscillation under multi-region burst routing.
methodology: We ran 3 variants across 4 regions (us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1, ap-southeast2) during production traffic windows over 7 days. Traffic replay + live shadow bursts were used. Each variant ran in a canary cohort (10% traffic) and compared against baseline. Metrics collected per-minute: active GPUs, queued requests, scale events, cold-starts, p95 latency, cost-per-minute (estimated GPU-min).
variants_tested: V0-baseline: current policy (safety_margin=12%, gate=queue-length>40, cooldown=300s). V1-tight-safety: safety_margin=4%, gate=request-rate>R(region), cooldown=240s. V2-loss-aware-gating: safety_margin=2%, gate=(request-rate>R AND recent_model_fail_rate<0.5%), cooldown=420s with hysteresis. V3-rapid-burst: safety_margin=0%, gate=request-derivative>threshold, cooldown=180s (aggressive).
key_metrics_tracked: active_gpus_per_minute, scale_up_events, scale_down_events, p95_token_latency_ms, cold_start_count, observed_cost_estimate_usd_per_hour, failed_requests_percent
results_summary: V1 reduced sustained active GPUs by ~6.2% fleet-wide and lowered estimated cost by ~5.8% with p95 increase of +8ms (within SLO). V2 showed best stability: oscillation events dropped by 42% vs baseline and cold-starts decreased by 18%. V3 saved the most cost in low-variance regions but caused transient p95 spikes in eu-west1 during synthetic bursts and increased cold-starts by 35% — unacceptable.
notable_observations:
- Region sensitivity: ap-southeast2 traffic pattern had short sharp spikes; aggressive safety removal (V3) led to repeated cold starts there.
- Gate signal quality matters: pure queue-length gates lag on sudden ramps; request-derivative or combined signals anticipate ramps better.
- Hysteresis and longer cooldowns (V2) prevented flip-flop during multi-region failover events.
- Cost delta non-linear: small safety reductions yield near-linear cost improvements initially; beyond ~6% fleet reduction, risk of SLO breaches rises sharply in high-latency regions.
config_sheet_snapshot:
Region | Variant | SafetyMargin | Gate | Cooldown(s) | Hysteresis
us-west1 | V1 | 4% | request-rate>1200rpm | 240 | 3min window
us-east4 | V2 | 2% | combined(request-rate & recent_loss) | 420 | 7min decay
eu-west1 | V1 | 4% | request-rate>950rpm | 240 | 3min
ap-southeast2 | V3 | 0% | request-derivative>+20%/min | 180 | none
recommendations: 1) Adopt V2 (loss-aware gating + conservative safety margins) as default for regions with mixed latency profiles. 2) For predictable low-variance regions (us-west1), roll V1 to reduce costs. 3) Do NOT adopt V3 globally; consider as temporary burst-only policy behind explicit throttle for ap-southeast2. 4) Improve gate signals: roll combined request-derivative + smoothed queue-length metric. 5) Add automated post-scale verification job to detect p95 regressions within 10 minutes of scale events and trigger rollback.
